memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Noah, a man of the soil, proceeded to plant a vineyard. When he drank some of its wine, he became drunk and lay uncovered inside his tent. - Gen 9:20-21 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is a hard and humbling passage. Noah - the righteous man, the one who walked with God, who obeyed everything God commanded, who was preserved through the flood - gets drunk and lies shamefully exposed in his tent. The great hero of faith falls into sin and disgrace. Scripture does not hide the failures of its heroes; it tells us the honest truth.

Why does the Bible include this? Because it is truthful about human nature, and because it points us away from trusting in people to trusting in God alone. Noah was righteous by grace, but he was not sinless. No one in Scripture is a perfect saviour - not Noah, not Abraham, not David. Every human hero has feet of clay.

There is a sobering warning here for all of us. If Noah, after such faithfulness and such a rescue, could fall, then none of us should think we are beyond temptation. "So, if you think you are standing firm, be careful that you don't fall!" (1 Cor 10:12). Past faithfulness is no guarantee against present failure. We must walk humbly and stay watchful all our lives.

But this passage also stirs a longing for a better Saviour - One who would not fail, not even once. Noah could bring the world through the flood, but he could not conquer sin in his own heart. Only Jesus, the truly righteous One, lived without sin and can save us completely (Heb 4:15). Our hope is never in flawed heroes, but in the flawless Christ.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Are you tempted to think past faithfulness makes you safe from falling?
- How does Noah's failure point you to your need for the sinless Saviour, Jesus?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, keep me humble and watchful, knowing that even the faithful can fall. Thank You that my hope is not in flawed heroes but in Jesus, the sinless Saviour who never fails. Guard my heart today.
